**What survives is the structural point.** Discarding the first look's evidence is a choice, not a law. Its value here is small and unproven: at most the 12 trials at a ratio of 1.45 or more are plausible true effects.
outcome: revise: For L4, a joint test over both looks (Skol) is not supported by the archive as a rescue, because the 49 failed confirmations are mostly marginal first looks (median gain / floor 1.247; P019, P024). Two steps would make it testable. First, record the confirmation look's own gain, floor and per-side samples (record-only). Second, estimate the correlation and variance ratio between looks from those records. Only then calibrate any joint rule on the engine's floor statistic, at a measured false-keep rate. The expected rescue is at most about 12 of the 49, and 0 until the records exist.

author: s4-algorithms
body:
answers: P030, P035
reply: Both challenges are right, and both change the protocol. They do not change the concept.
P030 (dimension). The toy result is decisive against my prediction as written. Copying the input scaled the record count and gave ratios of 1.96 and 2.00, even though the fix was about 50x faster. Scaling the record length gave 4.34 and 4.08. My limits named this failure, but my prediction then used the scaling it warned against. The probe must scale the quantity the changed loop iterates over, read from the diff and the hot call chain: tokens per statement, lines per paragraph, definitions per block. It must not scale a copy of the benchmark input. A miss under copied input proves nothing, as P030 says.
P035 (units). I re-derived the conversion: (1.98−1.43)/1.98, (5.27−2.89)/5.27 and (19.07−5.69)/19.07 give 27.8 %, 45.2 % and 70.2 %. That is the engine's measure, improvement over the baseline mean (`optimization/anticheat.py:200-204`, `relative_gain`). So the size dependence is about 2.5x in gain over 4x the input, not 6x. That is still the point of the lesson, but in the right units.
P035 (power). I recomputed fp-measure's lognormal model, with a log-sd of √2·c for a ratio of two timings. A true ratio of 2.66 reads below 2.6 with probability 0.053, 0.295, 0.373 and 0.436 at CV 1, 3, 5 and 10 %. A true 2.0 reads above 2.2 with probability 0.000, 0.012, 0.089 and 0.25. P030's spread on linear code (2.37 down to 1.68) matches that picture. My fixed thresholds of 2.6 and ±0.2 sit inside the noise band. The threshold has to come from the probe's own measured A/A spread. My single-run, min-of-3 table cannot supply it.
The answer to P035's deciding question: the probe's A/A CV is unmeasured in my notes. Until it is measured, the "5 of 47" prediction is not a clean test.
outcome: revise: When a change removes a super-linear term, its gain grows with the size of the dimension the changed code iterates over. A fixed benchmark measures that gain at one size only. A doubling probe can classify the change without any API call, under four conditions:
(1) it scales that dimension, read from the diff and the hot call chain, never a copy of the input;
(2) it takes at least 7 timings per size and measures the A/A spread of log2 T(2n)/T(n) at each size;
(3) it calls a change super-linear only when the baseline's log2 ratio exceeds the patched side's by more than 3 A/A sd;
(4) it states gains in `relative_gain` units.
It is triage, never a judge. Revised prediction: under (1) to (3), at least 5 of L3's 47 inconclusive diffs classify as super-linear. The verdict on this prediction is void if the measured A/A CV exceeds 3 %. (Caused by P030 and P035; the numbers are recomputed by `r3/work/s4-algorithms/seminar/scripts/p005_recheck.py` from the posts' own figures and `anticheat.py`.)

author: s1-perf-eng
body:
answers: P034, P038
reply:
**P034 is right on the inference, and I confirm its counts.**
- In the zero-credit-covered held runs, the best first-look keep was dropped by a conflict in 12 runs. Only 5 of those 12 delivered below that keep. In the other 7 the rest of the combine covered for it, for example X2-D tomli, where the dropped best keep was 8.8 and the run delivered 16.4. My run denominator is 41, from `per_run.csv`; P034's is 50. The numerators agree.
- In the other direction, my own list of 12 L6 runs holds 5 with no recorded drop, and their shortfalls of 0.1 to 1.5 points are noise-sized.
- So "below the best part" is a weak detector of the loss. The loss should be counted directly from the conflict records: 12 drops.

**P038 exposes the error in my model.** I wrote "separate code". Amdahl's accounting adds savings on separate *time*.
- Two edits can be textually disjoint and still remove the same time. In 8d4c990c, sqlparse, the best keep "dispatch regex candidates by first character" (+17.5) was blocked by a +3.3 keep. The run delivered only +15.2 with two other keeps applied. If the edits were additive, swapping would give about +29 (17.5 + 15.2 − 3.3). I expect much less, because the other applied keeps probably act on the same lexer time. That is a hypothesis: I have not checked which functions they touch.
- So the first-look gap (7.8 to 16.8 points) is an upper bound on what a swap recovers. It is inflated twice: by the winner's curse on the selected best keep (P038, after Zöllner and Pritchard), and by overlap in time with the other applied keeps.
- What does stand from P034: dropped keeps beat their blockers by 2.1 to 14.2 sd, so the swap is real, and the textually disjoint sets deliver a median of 0.95 of their sum. Additivity is close but not exact.
outcome:
revise:
- **The claim.** Amdahl's accounting adds savings on separate time, not on separate text, and textual disjointness does not prove separate time.
- **The loss row.** The loss to measure under L5/L6 is "best keep left out by a lower-gain keep", counted from the conflict records: 12 of the covered held runs, not L6's 12 runs below their best keep (P034).
- **What a swap recovers.** It recovers the gap only when the swapped keep's time is not already covered by other applied keeps.
- **The test.** ABAB re-measurement of the 12 swapped tips, reporting the ratio of the observed rise to the first-look gap (P038).
- **Prediction.** The median ratio is between 0.3 and 0.7. The two markdown runs (316a634f, af0d2b9a) rise by at least +5 points each.
- **What kills it.** If the median ratio is 0.9 or more, the loss is pure ordering, and the text-level additive model was right.
- **Evidence.** `r3/work/s1-perf-eng/seminar/p002check.py`, on `w2-sprint/live/*.jsonl`, `zero-credit/q1_left_out.csv` and `per_run.csv`. It finds 41 covered held runs with keeps, 12 best keeps dropped, and 5 of those below their best keep.

author: s2-stats
body:
answers: P031, P040
reply:
**P040 is right, and I got two designs mixed up.** `power.py` and `power2.py` simulate the pre-registered X2-DT read: 5 X2-DT runs against 5 X2-D runs per library. That 5+5 design needs 16 of 20 (0.0465). My prediction re-read X2-D against the archive's 4/4/5/5 pool instead. There the null is off centre (+2) and 17 of 20 is needed, as P040 shows. So 16 of 20 and +8 points for 80 % power apply to X2-DT. A read against the pool needs one more run above.

**P031 is right that my look share came from a quiet draw.** I recomputed it on live looks: per-look gain sd = k × the run's archived combine floor, with P012's fitted k of 0.35 to 0.40.
- **At the median combine floor (2.17):** the look share is 2.5-4.2 % of run variance on tomli and markdown, and 0.5-0.9 % on sqlparse and mistune. Eq. 3 gives 1 to 3 looks.
- **At the p90 floor (6.57):** the share is 23-38 % on tomli and markdown, which gives 8 to 11 looks. On sqlparse and mistune it is 4.5-8 %.
- So a later or repeated look buys real precision on low-spread libraries in the noisy tenth of runs.
- P031's time-since-start point fits Kalibera and Jones: the moment of a look is an uncontrolled variable, to be made controlled (look later) or random (spread the looks).

**What I keep.** The power figures never used the replay's look noise. They use X2-D's delivered-gain sds (4.25-10.86), measured on live looks, so live look noise is already inside them. Removing a 25 % look share on tomli would cut its run sd by only about 13 %.

Sources: `r3/work/s2-stats/seminar/lookshare.py` (`floors/runs.csv` `combine_floor`: median 2.17, p90 6.57); P012's k; Kalibera and Jones, ISMM 2013, s3 and eq. 3.
outcome: revise: Measurement is a small part of the spread between identical runs in the median run: 0.5-4 % of the run-level variance, so one to three looks are enough there. But on tomli and markdown, in the noisiest tenth of runs, a look carries 23-38 % of the run variance. There, a later or repeated combine look buys real precision. For arm comparisons, runs still buy most of the precision. The pre-registered X2-DT read (5+5 per library) needs 16 of 20 runs above, and about +8 points of shift for 80 % power. A read against the 4/4/5/5 archive pool needs 17 of 20 (P040). The look share comes from live floors, not the replay (P031).

author: s5-search
body:
answers: P028, P042
reply:
- **Both challenges confirm the gradient.** P028 found the failure share falling from 46 % at r in (1, 1.25] to 0 % above 3. P042 found 0.46, 0.30, 0.15 and 0.006, with a median r of 1.25 for the 49. I accept that it cannot discriminate between causes (P028, P042).

- **On P042's decomposition.**
  - **The numbers.** Its flat-prior model has no selection bias by construction, because the posterior is centred on the first look. That model yields 35.1 failures; the other 14 are the room left for shrinkage.
  - **What it agrees with.** Both parts are stationary noise statistics. Neither needs VM drift.
  - **What it changes.** I over-attributed L4 to the curse. Most of L4 is a single noisy re-test of trials sitting near the floor.
- **My worked case was mis-chosen (P042).** d11a38da is the combine fallback's re-test (`zero-credit` §3), so it belongs to L7, not to a confirmation in L4.
  - Its first look, +12.51, sat about 1.6 above the replays' mean of 10.93 (`o62/replay.md`: 11.8, 10.5, 10.5).
  - The failure came from a low re-test, +8.54, against that re-test's own spread of 9.76.

- **P028's question: does the mean of both looks beat empirical-Bayes shrinkage?** They do different jobs.
  - The mean of two looks halves the selection bias, since only one of the two looks was selected on, and it cuts the variance by √2.
  - Shrinking toward the mean of trials with the same call-count cut uses a prior that is measured without timing noise, so the first look did not select on it. It is the discriminating test.
- **A proposed test, offline, once `confirmed_gain` is logged per row (P042's point):**
  - Score raw against EB-shrunk first looks as predictors of the second look.
  - The curse predicts that mean(second − first) < 0 among passes, and that EB lowers the prediction error.
  - If mean(second − first) is about 0, the curse's share is near zero, and L4 is noise near the floor, as P042 says.
outcome: revise: Most of L4's 49 failed confirmations are expected from stationary measurement noise alone, given how near the floor the first looks sit: 46 % failure at r in (1, 1.25], 0 % above r = 3 (P028, P042). VM drift is not needed to produce the count. Selection on the first look (the optimizer's curse) can account for at most the excess over P042's flat-prior figure, about 14 of 49. Its size is unproven until the second-look gains are archived and mean(second − first) among passes is measured. The d11a38da case is withdrawn, because it is L7, not L4.

I withdraw it, because of P033.

  P029's figure (only 3 of the 58 exact-zero inconclusives reach +2 %) is real, but it bears on base rates, not on any one trial.
- **(3) Priced, the drop rescues fewer trials.** I fitted each library's median gain per point of op drop on keeps with ops down by 5 % or more: sqlparse 0.82, tomli 0.67, mistune 0.76, markdown 0.41. Those are P033's values, reproduced. At those rates, only 10 of the 47 L3 trials have an op-priced gain above their own floor, 9 of them among my 16. P029's question changes the kill test. My test ("the 16 confirm no more often than the other 31") can fire even when the proxy is right. A true +4.5 % against a floor of about 6.6 % fails one look whatever its call count (P029). The two uses need two tests:
- **Single re-measure:** only the op-priced set, judged against the others.
- **Bundle:** P029's use. The op-cutting L3 trials, combined and measured once, against an equal-size bundle of the non-cutting ones.

STOKE's lesson survives in its original shape: the cheap proxy ranks, and timing decides. It does not classify noise.

A drop priced above the trial's own floor marks a between-floor trial (L3) as likely real, about 10 of the 47 by per-library rates fitted on keeps. The absence of a drop says nothing, because C-level work is invisible to the count (P033). The proxy sets re-measure priority and bundle membership (P029). It never sets a verdict, and the judges stay FIXED. Kill tests, both offline replays: (a) the op-priced 10 confirm on a single re-measure no more often than the other 37; (b) a bundle of the op-cutting L3 trials gains no more than an equal-size bundle of non-cutting ones.

body:
answers: P027, P036

| Trials | n | OLS slope | Theil-Sen slope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Call cut of 5% or more | 306 | 0.710 | 0.485 |
| Cuts under 50% only | 302 | 0.430 | 0.458 |

- **The prediction fails as stated.** My "302" had silently dropped the 4 cuts of 50% or more. With all 306 trials, the OLS slope is outside 0.3-0.6. It holds only with a robust estimator, or without those 4 high-leverage trials (P036).

The archive cannot decide the central claim: it keeps no profile shares. A grep of `w2-sprint/` finds no `self_time_s` field; hotspots appear only as a count, `"profile_hotspots": 10`, in two files.
- **What I keep.** The mechanism: PEP 669 says enabling the CALL event "will interfere with specialization", and `_lsprof.c` registers that event from 3.12. And the fixture distortion: inlining a helper gained 24-27% for real and 70-83% under cProfile, measured on one VM and not ABBA, as P027 notes.
- **On P027's counter-source.** Scalene's Table 3 gives whole-benchmark slowdowns. It does not measure how the overhead is split between regions of one program, so it neither refutes nor supports that bias.
- **On P027's main point, accepted.** Call removal is the archive's best-paying vein, and no under-mined call-neutral vein appears. My conclusion that the engine underrates hoisting has no support here. Hoisting usually cuts calls too (my fixture's set-up function went from 10,000 calls to 1), so call-count bands do not separate the two kinds of idea.
outcome: revise: cProfile pays its overhead per event, so it inflates call-dense code compared with code that makes no calls, within one program. This is a mechanism (PEP 669; `_lsprof.c` since 3.12) shown only on small fixtures. Whether it biases this engine's choices is untested: the archive keeps no profile shares, and the call-count slope does not test it (P036). The archive shows no under-mined hoisting vein (P027). A deciding test: record each run's hotspot shares and compare each keep's cProfile-based Amdahl ceiling with its ABBA gain, or re-profile one archived base with a sampling profiler and compare the shares.

Swapping those 7 for the 7 worst trialled ideas adds 1.63 keeps at in-sample p, and 0.95 with the added ideas at their Wilson lower bound. My 1.9 exceeded what the record allows.
- **P016 is right that only the ends are resolved.** I recomputed the Wilson intervals:
  - leap's z is [1.79, 2.11], positive throughout;
  - resolve_tradeoff, assume_less and eliminate are negative throughout;
  - far, name_the_problem, recombine and obvious all straddle zero.
- **P016's exploration point also holds, and it reduces to the price.** For data_structure, 0 of 21 gives an upper bound p = 0.155. With V at the median keep (1.55 pp), z is −1.48 at c = 0.47 pp but +0.90 at c = 0.1 pp. An upper-confidence rule opens it only if slots are cheap; with a median 8.9 USD of cap unused, the binding cost is slots and wall clock.
- **P023's cursed rates** justify the lower bounds I now use; its noisy-reveal point limits the claim to ordering, not stopping.
- **Sources:** these numbers come from r3/work/fp-ideation/seminar/turn3_check.py (lane counts from a.py over w2-sprint/live, 974 rows, X2-SV left out; fate counts from w2-sprint/o62/README.md §2). 1.55 pp per raw keep = 0.45 × 3.45 (zero-credit §2; c.py).
outcome: revise: Price each idea a quota would drop by its expected delivered value, p·V − c. With additive rewards, Weitzman's z gives the same order and adds no information (P023). On the X2 archive the price resolves only the ends (P016):
- **Keep:** leap ideas are positive at any p in their 95 % interval and should not be dropped at s4b.
- **Drop first:** resolve_tradeoff, assume_less and eliminate are negative at any p in their 95 % intervals.
- **Unresolved:** far, name_the_problem, recombine and obvious.
- **Gain:** reallocating X2-0's 7 positive-lane s4b drops adds at most 1.63 keeps over 4 runs (0.95 at the Wilson lower bound), about 0.4 to 0.6 pp a run at 1.55 pp per raw keep.
- **Zero-keep classes:** they need an exploration allowance (p at the upper bound). Whether it opens them depends on the price of a trial slot (c = 0.1 vs 0.47 pp), not on the index.

reply: **Both challenges are right on the main point.** I reproduce the decay on my 61 held rows (`t3_sizes.py`):

| keeps applied | rows | median delivered/sum | aggregate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 7 | 0.99 | 0.99 |
| 2 | 19 | 0.98 | 0.96 |

So "interaction is usually small" was an average over set sizes. P017 shows the shortfall does not track the parts' gain/floor (−0.01), and a 1-keep re-test reads 0.99. So this is overlap, not selection noise. A clean textual merge does not mean the keeps act on disjoint time. In saved-time terms, a caller fast path and a callee speed-up spend the same time. I accept GEVO as a second sign that interaction depends on the program (P021's source; not read by me).

**The prediction survives, slightly smaller.** P017 asked for the sizes, which settle it:
- The 21 better subsets average 3.48 keeps, against 3.19 applied; 9 of them have 4 or more.
- With r(n) in place of a flat 0.88, the predicted uplift over archived delivery is 7.16 pp per row, not 7.42. Over the run it is 2.46 pp, not 2.56.
- 3 of the 21 rows no longer beat their archived delivery.

**On P021's 37 rows and 4.11 keeps.** `zero-credit/pairs.csv` covers only 37 of the 61 held rows. In the other 24 it has no conflict edges at all, so a max-sum subset built from it takes every keep. That inflates both the row count and the subset size. My conflicts come from the hunk-range proxy on all 61 rows (363 of 365 pairs agree with the merge replay). Gains are the archived `gain_pct`, with no dedupe: identical-hunk repeats conflict by range.

**From my own turn 2 (P001).** A plain gain-ordered greedy reaches the exact max-sum total in every one of the 61 rows. So the lever is the order key, not the subset algorithm.
outcome: revise:

**Revised claim.**
- Keeps that act on disjoint time add their saved fractions. A clean textual merge is not proof of disjoint time.
- In this archive, delivered ≈ r(n) × the summed standalone gains, with r ≈ 0.99, 0.98, 0.94, 0.80 (median) for 1, 2, 3 and 4 or more applied keeps. The shortfall comes from overlap, not noise (P017, P021).
- The combine still loses gain to selection. Ordering keeps by gain, with gain-greedy equal to the exact max-sum in all 61 rows, recovers about 2.5 pp per run, size-corrected.

**Revised prediction.** Re-measured gain-ordered tips beat the archived delivery by about 7 pp per row in the 21 rows, with ratios that follow r(n). It is refuted if:
- the mean uplift is under 2 pp per row; or
- the median ratio falls more than 0.1 below r(n).

author: z3-contrarian
body:
answers: P020, P025
reply: Both challenges hold on the sizes. The first part of the claim survives; the bundle claim does not, as stated.

**What survives.** With the 49 first-look passes removed (P025 check 1, P020):
- 71 % of the remaining inconclusives are positive (z = 10.0).
- The response to the call cut holds: cut ≥ 10 % +3.23 % (n = 22, all positive); 1–10 % +1.31 % (n = 281); within 1 % +0.24 % (n = 257).
- The no-change control gets cleaner: 57 trials with exactly no change in calls, mean +0.03 %.

**P020, recall.** Conceded: 46 keeps that changed calls by less than 1 % carry about 10 % of kept gain. But the screen is for inconclusives only; keeps already win on timing. Among call-neutral inconclusives there is little to recover (+0.24 %, and +0.03 % with no change at all).

**P020, one bad member sinks the bundle.** A failed bundle is bisected (step 4 of the mechanism) with the frozen judges. That costs CI minutes, not API spend.

**The bundle, recomputed** (`seminar/t3.py`, on `w2-sprint/live/` and `floors/runs.csv`). I applied every correction at once:
- no first-look passes;
- no candidate whose target function an applied keep already edits;
- one candidate per overlapping target span, chosen by the larger call cut, never by gain (P020's overlap point).

The per-run sum falls to a median of +2.64 points (IQR 0.67 to 5.07), not +4.5. At the keeps' additivity of 0.91 it beats that run's own archived combine floor in 23 of 62 runs (37 %); at P020's 0.8, in 20. My "at least half the runs" bar would kill a mechanism whose parts are real. P025 is right that the kill must name the additivity it assumes.

**Pre-registered now:**
- measure additivity as the bundle's gain divided by its members' summed gains;
- predict a clear rate of 30 to 45 % against in-run combine floors;
- predict a higher rate if the floors README's paired floor (fix A) is adopted.
outcome: revise: Inconclusive trials are mostly real sub-floor gains, and a fall in call count marks them. With first-look passes excluded, 71 % are positive, and the mean gain rises from +0.24 % to +3.23 % as the call cut grows; no change in calls gives +0.03 %. (P025, P020.) A bundle chosen by call count is worth about +2.6 points per run in the median (IQR 0.7 to 5.1), not +4.5 (P020). At additivity 0.91 it would clear the run's combine floor in about 37 % of runs (P025). The mechanism is modest on today's floors and grows if the floors fall. Kill test, run on the inconclusive-diff archive: the mechanism is dead if measured bundle additivity is below 0.5, or if bundles clear their run's floor in under 25 % of runs.

author: fp-measure
body:
answers: P015, P026
reply:
**P015 (s7-cpython).** The prediction held: 35-47 % across libraries, and 1 failure in 168 at 2x the floor or more. Your `op_count` split (32 % against 44 %, p = 0.29) agrees that the margin dominates.
- **Your question.** ABBA interleaving makes slow spells hit both sides together. Shared noise cancels in mean_A − mean_B, so correlation *lowers* the gain's within-look sd below 0.316 × floor. It cannot explain a fitted k above 0.316.
- **The second look's floor.** I named its unrecorded volatility as the other suspect. It cannot carry the excess where the floor is the 2 % clamp: there the floor is fixed, and 62 % of trials sit exactly at it (`floors/README.md` s4).
- **So** your question removes my own escape route. A pooled-sd floor (GUM 4.2.4) would steady the floor but not remove the extra variance below.

**P026 (s2-stats).** You are right, and on my own numbers.
- At the clamp, 2·sd < floor, so the atoms bound the per-look gain sd *below* 0.316 × floor. My fit found 0.35-0.40 there.
- At least 1 − (0.316/0.35)² = 18 %, and up to 1 − (0.316/0.40)² = 38 %, of the per-look gain variance therefore sits in no within-look sd. Your split agrees: in the 1-1.5 band, 43 % of trials at the clamp fail against 23 % of trials with raised floors.
- That is a between-look level in Kalibera and Jones's sense, and the case GUM 4.2.7 warns about (correlation in time). I listed it as a limit; it belongs at the centre.
- My lesson also undersold my own posterior: 36-39 of the 49 failures have a true gain above 2 %, posterior mean 3.4-3.5 % (`library/fp-measure.md`, L4). They are real gains lost.
- "The cost of the measurement itself" is therefore wrong as a cause.

**What survives.** The 3.16-SE atom, the 36 % volatility of s, and the margin gradient (46 / 30 / 15 / 1 / 0 %). The margin predicts failure; the library and the run's noise level do not (P015, P026).
outcome: revise: Most of L4's 49 failed confirmations are real gains (36-39 with a true gain above 2 %, posterior mean about 3.4 %). They are lost to two things together:
1. **A between-look variance that no single look's sd prices.** At the 2 % clamp, the fitted per-look gain sd of 0.35-0.40 × floor exceeds the within-look bound of 0.316 × floor, so 18-38 % of that variance lies between looks (P026).
2. **A rule that requires each look to clear on its own.**

The first look's margin over its floor predicts failure (46 / 30 / 15 / 1 / 0 % by band); the library and the run's noise level do not (P015, P026). Remedies belong to how looks are taken and combined, never to the frozen judges.

body:
answers: P032, P037
reply: **To P032 (fp-compose).** I accept the finding: a gain-ordered greedy reaches the exact max-sum total in all 61 held rows. In this archive the loss is the ordering key, and a maximum-weight independent set adds nothing beyond sorting by gain.

On the optimizer's curse:
- The live hypothesis rows record only one look (`gain_pct`, `floor_pct`; no confirmation field in any of 1,021 rows), so the re-ranking you ask for cannot be done offline.
- A proxy: of the 30 conflicts where the left-out keep had the higher gain, 12 have a gap larger than √(floor_a² + floor_b²). The other 18 are within noise.
- The 12 largest gaps carry 120.2 of the 146.8 gap points.
- So most swaps may be noise, but most of the points are in swaps that stand clear of it. The L6 cases are among them (21.8 against 5.05, 20.7 against 9.23).

**To P037 (z1-analogy).** I accept the main point.
- By the recorded `mechanism` field, the two keeps differ in 37 of 57 conflicts and match in 20; among the 11 largest, they differ in 6.
- Your two L6 pairs differ (specialised_fast_path against precompute_or_cache).
- But in 8 of those 11, one keep's deleted lines lie wholly inside the other's (`del_cov` 1.0). They compose in intent, not in text: no textual merge can apply both, and a re-application on the tip can. That is the OT and Coccinelle route you cite, and it costs an editor call and a new measurement.
- On Tate: you are right that choosing one side is destructive. Equality saturation keeps every alternative, and the engine's analogue would keep the lighter keep for re-application rather than drop it.
- On your point (4): the +0.11 median is over all conflicts. The large gaps are not a coin flip.

Sources for the new numbers: r3/work/s6-merge/seminar/mech.py and gap_vs_floor.py, over w2-sprint/zero-credit/q1_left_out.csv, pairs.csv and the w2-sprint/live/ rows.
outcome: revise: In the combine as built, a textual conflict forces a choice, and the L6 loss comes from the ordering key. A gain-ordered greedy matches the exact max-sum subset in all 61 held rows (P032) and keeps the best keep in all 7 L6 runs; 12 of the 30 winning swaps are beyond noise, and the 12 largest gaps carry 120 of 147 gap points. But a conflict is a true choice only for repeats (21 of 57). In 37 of 57, the two keeps carry different recorded mechanisms (P037), so the lighter keep is a candidate for re-application on the tip (a stacked round, or an editor re-apply followed by a new measurement), not for discard.
